homeDescription: Follow a missing hour through the rain-soaked streets of 1980s Blackwater City as detective Mara Vale and a cast of other playable characters. Investigate crime scenes, unravel unsettling puzzles, survive ordinary shifts gone wrong, and trace the anonymous audio recordings left behind by the Signal Keeper.
mechanicsIntro: Four systems define a run through Blackwater City: evidence-based crime-scene investigation, anonymous audio recordings, multiple playable perspectives, and an analog-horror presentation built on low-poly spaces and uneasy late-night routines.

about: Midnight Evidence is an original fictional horror adventure imagined by Hollow Signal and its publishing partner Lantern House. Set in a fading 1980s Blackwater City, it follows detective Mara Vale and her partner Ellis Reed as they investigate a missing hour in the emergency records. An anonymous sender leaves a trail of recorded voices and background sounds that do not match the official timeline.

The story concept emphasizes atmosphere, observation and tension. Players compare crime-scene evidence, work through environmental puzzles and switch into other perspectives across diners, cinemas, radio rooms and deserted railway platforms. Familiar spaces become unsettling through changes in routine, restrained dialogue and a deliberately simple low-poly visual language.

This is a working website demonstration with an original game world, rather than a released commercial game. The archive organizes its fictional material with the same care as a practical guide: beginning routes first, optional story revelations on their own pages, and clear labels for unfinished reference notes. All game information, studio names and illustrations here are original demonstration content. No release, sales figures, user reviews or real-world partnerships are claimed. The case notes share a consistent fictional timeline, with observations kept separate from final revelations. aboutSections.title: Blackwater City’s story and setting
paragraphs: Mara Vale and her partner Ellis Reed begin with a discrepancy in the emergency records: an entire hour has disappeared. Witnesses remember a train, a radio broadcast and a customer arriving after closing time, yet none of those events appear in the official log. Anonymous recordings bring the detectives back to places that seem ordinary in daylight.

The story moves between the investigation and the people who were working that night. A receipt, a screening schedule and a station clock become different ways of describing the same missing hour. Each chapter adds context before asking you to decide whether a memory or a written record deserves your trust.

aboutSections.title: How the investigation plays
paragraphs: The fictional game combines small locations, conversations and environmental puzzles. Read the current objective, examine objects from more than one angle and compare their details with your notebook. Most puzzles begin with an inconsistency you can see or hear rather than a code hidden without explanation. A changed label can matter as much as a locked door.

Civilian sections put familiar routines first: finish a diner order, inspect the projection room or complete a railway maintenance round. Those modest tasks establish how a place normally works. When the routine changes, you already understand what is wrong. The concept emphasizes atmosphere and patient observation instead of fighting enemies or managing a large inventory.

aboutSections.title: Playable characters and performance notes
paragraphs: Mara follows the case from the precinct, while Ellis checks records against the witnesses’ accounts. Nina Hart remembers the diner through orders and receipts. Cass Rowan recognizes a mislabeled film reel, and Owen Park knows which station equipment should remain switched off overnight. Their practical knowledge reveals details the detectives could otherwise miss.

The cast notes describe original fictional roles and performance directions. They do not claim that real actors have recorded dialogue or that a commercial game has been produced. Read the character previews for each location and perspective; unfinished profiles stay in the guide index until a full article is available.

aboutSections.title: The opening route and complete story concept
paragraphs: The imagined opening covers the precinct, the late-night diner and Blackwater Station. It introduces the notebook, object inspection and the first anonymous recording before the case expands into a cinema and a radio room. The opening is designed to be readable without learning the final explanation for the missing hour.

Later chapters revisit those locations through other viewpoints. Information that looked like background decoration becomes evidence when it appears in a second account. This website demonstrates the guide structure for that concept; it does not provide a playable demo, a download, a release date or a storefront for an unreleased game.

aboutSections.title: Platforms, languages and project materials
paragraphs: The design outline imagines a single-player PC adventure with readable objectives, optional subtitles and simple interaction controls. It is a creative brief rather than a statement of system requirements. No Windows installer, console edition, mobile port or actual language support is claimed by the fictional project.

The working guide website offers English, German, Brazilian Portuguese, Spanish and Simplified Chinese. Each version shares the same layout and uses its own written content. Illustrations are stored locally as original SVG scenes, and article text comes from MDX files rather than a remote service or copied game assets.
